correctness.rationale: Using Wang–Zenger Lemma 6, each G(alpha) is equivalent to R_alpha subset R; Lemma 5 fixes converse composition. The identity R_x=R makes G(x) valid. I independently recomputed R_alpha for all seven words on each of the six explicit frames (world sets of size two or three); their six nontrivial truth vectors are the six standard basis vectors. Hence each ordered cross-implication has an actual finite counterframe, which suffices universally; no finite exhaustive search is misused to prove a universal inclusion. The convention reversing composition order for x-bar words was checked against the source.
residual_risks: The conclusion relies on the precise Wang–Zenger generalized path-condition semantics and converse-composition convention; it is not a claim about conjunctions or longer words.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial bounded implication poset for generalized path conditions is a natural structural baseline for choosing independent modal frame axiom families: all six possible single-word constraints really are independent. The concrete size-at-most-three countermodels give minimal-scale negative information useful when constructing proof systems; the claim is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a claim of larger calculus consequences.
residual_risks: Because the range contains only seven words, its importance is as a first structural boundary; it does not establish longer-word classifications or decision procedures.

final_claim: For seven generalized path words of length at most two in non-contingency semantics, G(x) is universally true and the other six conditions are pairwise incomparable on all Kripke frames.
limitations: Single conditions generated by words of length at most two only; not conjunctions, longer words or calculus completeness.
